A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AdaptVision research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-B. Pages 4-15 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; differences on pages 1-3 are metadata edits and layout reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original AdaptVision benchmark results in Tables 1-2, inference-time measurements, reward and optimization ablations, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, inference-time measurements, ablations, and qualitative case studies, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The low-resolution input, adaptive bounding-box tool, reward design, and Decoupled Turn Policy Optimization procedure in Section 4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VisionThink training data and nine evaluation benchmarks listed in Section 5.1. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same vanilla and down-sampled Qwen2.5-VL baselines, SparseVLM, FastV, VisionZip, and both VisionThink variants. The AdaptVision without DTPO comparison in Table 1 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1-5.2 and Appendix A.2 retain the same model, dataset splits, metrics, training settings, and inference procedure. The static baselines' 50% retention setting and appendix comparisons at 50% and 70% are unchanged.

E4.justification: The reward ablations, GRPO-versus-DTPO training comparisons, and tool-use analyses in Figures 5-6 are identical. The main-text and appendix case studies in Figures 7-9 are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting in the result tables and training plots is unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Tables 1-2 report the same 97.9% average performance relative to the vanilla model at 33% visual-token consumption, and Figure 4 retains the reported 1.67x overall speedup.

T1.justification: The GRPO formulation, policy and reward definitions, DTPO objective, and advantage calculations in Sections 3-4 are unchanged. Equation spacing and placement on page 3 change without altering the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive visual acquisition, DTPO training, and performance with reduced visual-token consumption.

C2.justification: The explanations of optimization stability and adaptive tool use are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations: one visual tool, fixed initial quarter resolution, and a maximum of two reasoning turns.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical prompts, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and training and inference details. The code/model link and training-data access information are unchanged; the added author emails provide general contact information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The discussion contrasting AdaptVision with fixed-ratio compression and VisionThink merely flows across different page boundaries.

P1.justification: The author affiliation changes from Tencent AI Lab to Tencent Hunyuan, author email addresses are added, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added email line shifts Figure 1 and nearby content downward and changes column/page breaks and equation spacing across pages 1-3. Figure content, captions, and tables are unchanged; pages 4-15 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliation and contact metadata with modest layout reflow. The methodology, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged, including the appendices, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
